studies.label: Basal-condition physiology — v2ecoli baseline vs experimental literature
Re-measure biomass yield on a recorded commit, and discriminate one defect from two
Does the model's own aerobic-to-anaerobic yield drop match biology?

nodes.label: The baseline ensemble makes 0.826 gDW of biomass per gram of glucose consumed...
nodes.statement: The baseline ensemble makes 0.826 gDW of biomass per gram of glucose consumed — 1.86× the top of the measured band (0.355–0.444) and 1.54× the first-principles ceiling of 0.538. No carbon- and energy-balanced cell can exceed that ceiling, so this is a model defect, not a calibration mismatch. The dispersion is tight (CV 1.55% across 20 cells), so it is a systematic property of the model rather than noise. Carbon is nonetheless conserved at baseline — implied biomass carbon ≈ 0.457 gC/gDW is physically plausible — which locates the defect on the energetic side: the ensemble barely respires (O₂:glucose ≈ 0.09, CO₂:glucose ≈ 0.33, RQ ≈ 3.6 against ~1 for full oxidation), so almost no glucose carbon is burned for maintenance and ATP, and nearly all of it is retained as biomass.

nodes.label: On a run whose commit is recorded, the baseline makes 0.831 gDW per gram of g...
nodes.statement: On a run whose commit is recorded, the baseline makes 0.831 gDW per gram of glucose - 1.87x the top of the measured band and 1.55x the first-principles ceiling - and the run shows no sign of the gross carbon imbalance that appears under a binding uptake cap. Implied biomass carbon comes out at 0.455 gC/gDW, an ordinary value, against a binding-cap condition where closure degrades to 7.93. The comparison that carries this is RELATIVE: two conditions of the same model behaving qualitatively differently. A single mass-bookkeeping defect would break conservation in both. What the baseline fails to do is respire: O2:glucose is 0.096 and RQ is 3.43 against ~1 for full oxidation, so 94.5% of glucose carbon is retained as biomass and almost none is burned for maintenance and ATP. The violation is therefore energetic in origin - the cell builds biomass it never pays the ATP cost for - and is a different failure from the carbon creation the binding cap triggers. Two defects, not one.

nodes.label: The fresh run gives Yxs 0.8313 against the committed fixture's 0.8257, a diff...
nodes.statement: The fresh run gives Yxs 0.8313 against the committed fixture's 0.8257, a difference of 0.67% - well inside the ensemble CV of 1.44%. Growth rate 0.851 vs 0.814 and glucose uptake 4.81 vs 5.14 are likewise close. So the fixture's headline number is reproducible on current main even though its provenance was never recorded, and the first_principles_violation verdict standing since 2026-06-17 is not an artefact of a stale or unattributable bake.
